records.title: Determine which player goes first.
records.text: 7.5. ### Determine which player goes first.

records.title: You and your Rival agree upon and then execute a method to randomly choose a player.
records.text:
7.5.1. You and your Rival agree upon and then execute a method to randomly choose a player.

> **TIP:** We recommend both players roll a d20, and choose the player that rolled the higher number. If there’s a tie, both players roll again.

records.title: The player chosen via the random method decides and indicates to their Rival whether they will go first or second.
records.text: 7.5.2. The player chosen via the random method decides and indicates to their Rival whether they will go first or second.

records.title: Shuffle your main deck.
records.text: 7.6. ### Shuffle your main deck.

records.title: You may shuffle by any method you want, as long as it’s timely and properly randomized.
records.text: 7.6.1. You may shuffle by any method you want, as long as it’s timely and properly randomized.

records.title: When both players finish shuffling, present your deck to your Rival.
records.text: 7.6.2. When both players finish shuffling, present your deck to your Rival. Your Rival may “cut the deck” for you, if they choose.

records.title: Place your main deck in the deck area of your playmat.
records.text: 7.6.3. Place your main deck in the deck area of your playmat.

records.title: Randomize and place your Legends.
records.text: 7.7. ### Randomize and place your Legends.

records.title: Shuffle and randomize your 3 Legend cards with the same randomization method you used for your main deck.
records.text: 7.7.1. Shuffle and randomize your 3 Legend cards with the same randomization method you used for your main deck.

records.title: When both players finish shuffling, present your Legends face-down to your Rival.
records.text: 7.7.2. When both players finish shuffling, present your Legends face-down to your Rival. Your Rival may “cut the deck” of Legends for you, if they choose.

records.title: Place all 3 Legend cards face-down in your Legends area.
records.text: 7.7.3. Place all 3 Legend cards face-down in your Legends area.

records.title: The player going first spends their 2 left-most Legends.
records.text: 7.7.4. The player going first spends their 2 left-most Legends. These two Legends don’t ready on the starting turn.

records.title: Place your Gig dice in the fixer area.
records.text: 7.8. ### Place your Gig dice in the fixer area.

records.title: From the bottom up, place your d4, d6, d8, d10, d12, and then d20 in your fixer area.
records.text: 7.8.1. From the bottom up, place your d4, d6, d8, d10, d12, and then d20 in your fixer area.

records.title: Draw 6 cards.
records.text: 7.9. ### Draw 6 cards.

records.title: Draw 6 cards from the top of your deck and add them to your hand.
records.text: 7.9.1. Draw 6 cards from the top of your deck and add them to your hand. This is your “opening hand.”

records.title: You have up to one (1) opportunity to mulligan your opening hand.
records.text: 7.9.2. You have up to one (1) opportunity to mulligan your opening hand. The player going first must declare whether or not they will mulligan and if so, complete it, before the second player may declare and execute their own mulligan.

records.title: After looking at your starting hand (but before the game begins), you may use your mulligan by following these steps.
records.text: 7.9.3. After looking at your starting hand (but before the game begins), you may use your mulligan by following these steps.

records.title: Tell your Rival that you’re using your mulligan.
records.text: 7.9.3.1. Tell your Rival that you’re using your mulligan.

records.title: Return your full opening hand to your deck, then shuffle the deck via the same method you used in {7.6}.
records.text: 7.9.3.2. Return your full opening hand to your deck, then shuffle the deck via the same method you used in 7.6.

records.title: Draw 6 cards from the top of your deck and add them to your hand.
records.text: 7.9.3.3. Draw 6 cards from the top of your deck and add them to your hand. This is your new opening hand.

records.title: Always resolve as much of an effect as possible.
records.text: 10.2.1. Always resolve as much of an effect as possible. See GOLDEN RULES > Resolve as Much as Possible.

records.title: If part of an effect is invalid, ignore the invalid part and resolve as much of the remaining effect as possible.
records.text: 10.6.2. If part of an effect is invalid, ignore the invalid part and resolve as much of the remaining effect as possible.

records.title: If an effect becomes invalid after it activates or becomes pending, still resolve as much of the effect as possible.
records.text: 10.10. If an effect becomes invalid after it activates or becomes pending, still resolve as much of the effect as possible.

records.title: If an effect requires you to choose a specific number of targets, you must choose that number of targets.
records.text: 10.31.2. If an effect requires you to choose a specific number of targets, you must choose that number of targets. If you can’t, choose as many valid targets as possible up to that number instead.

records.title: Search
records.text: 11.13. ### Search

records.title: “Search” is a game action in which you look at a designated amount of cards.
records.text: 11.13.1. “Search” is a game action in which you look at a designated amount of cards.

records.title: When an effect says “Search X” (where X is a number), look at X number of cards from the top of your deck.
records.text: 11.13.1.1. When an effect says “Search X” (where X is a number), look at X number of cards from the top of your deck.

records.title: Once you fulfill any “Search” requirements, if the card does not tell you where to place the cards afterward, return…
records.text:
11.13.2. Once you fulfill any “Search” requirements, if the card does not tell you where to place the cards afterward, return the cards to their original location in the same order.

> **EXAMPLE:** A Legend’s effect text reads “When a friendly equipped Unit is defeated, search the top 2 cards of your deck and trash 1.” You look at the top 2 cards of your deck, move one to the trash, and place the other one back on the top of your deck.

records.title: While searching cards in an area, the cards still count towards the total number of cards in that area.
records.text:
11.13.3. While searching cards in an area, the cards still count towards the total number of cards in that area. The card does not leave the area until (and unless) you move it to a new game area.

> **EXAMPLE:** An effect requires you to search the top 3 cards of your deck. Your deck currently contains only 2 cards. You search as many cards as you can (2), but you do not immediately lose; because you did not draw them, they’re still in your deck.

records.title: When an effect allows you to search one of your hidden areas for a specific card or criteria, if you fail to find any…
records.text: 11.13.4. When an effect allows you to search one of your hidden areas for a specific card or criteria, if you fail to find anything, you don’t have to show the hidden information to the Rival player. See Hidden Areas.

records.title: When you search a hidden area for a specific target(s) and you’re not obligated to reveal the searched cards, you may…
records.text:
11.13.4.1. When you search a hidden area for a specific target(s) and you’re not obligated to reveal the searched cards, you may purposely fail to find any or all target(s).

> **EXAMPLE:** An effect says “Search the top 3 cards of your deck. Reveal a Gear and add it to your hand. Bottom-deck the rest.” When you search the top 3 cards of your deck, you find 2 Gear cards. But, because your deck is a hidden area, you may choose not to reveal any of them, and bottom-deck all 3 cards.

records.title: Reveal
records.text: 11.14. ### Reveal

records.title: "Reveal" is a game action in which you show designated cards to your Rival.
records.text: 11.14.1. "Reveal" is a game action in which you show designated cards to your Rival.

records.title: Revealing a card is not removing it from the designated area unless specified after effect resolution.
records.text: 11.14.2. Revealing a card is not removing it from the designated area unless specified after effect resolution. (Such as adding a revealed card to hand.)

records.title: While revealing a card, make sure it is shown in a face up position, such that either player may read the card.
records.text: 11.14.3. While revealing a card, make sure it is shown in a face up position, such that either player may read the card.

records.title: Once a revealed card has been placed back face-down, it is hidden and can no longer be looked at unless otherwise spe…
records.text: 11.14.4. Once a revealed card has been placed back face-down, it is hidden and can no longer be looked at unless otherwise specified.

records.title: The effect attached to the [CALL] trigger enters pending when you reveal the Called Legend.
records.text: 11.18.2. The effect attached to the [CALL] trigger enters pending when you reveal the Called Legend.
